## What DiffPTM does

A modified peptide's intensity changes when the modification changes **and** when its
protein changes. DiffPTM separates the two questions:

* **differential PTM abundance (DPA)**: does the site change between conditions, whatever
  the reason?
* **differential PTM usage (DPU)**: does the site change *relative to its protein*? This
  needs the total-proteome table and is the test DiffPTM is built for.

Three statistical methods answer the usage question and can be run side by side on the same
processed data: the single model (limma; paired when the PTM and proteome samples share
their names), MSstatsPTM (model then correct) and msqrob2PTM (correct then model). They
give the same usage fold changes but different standard errors. By default the single model
pairs each site with its protein sample by sample (per-site paired single model, the limma
analysis of the within-sample differences); the consensus version, which shares one
correlation between all sites, gains degrees of freedom but assumes that a site and its
protein vary alike, which `dpu_diagnostics()` checks. MSstatsPTM is the choice when the two
fractions do not come from the same samples.

Every usage test assumes that, without a usage change, a site follows its protein one to one.
`usage_beta_check()` refits the usage model with the protein term scaled by 0.8 and 1.2 and
flags the calls that do not survive; calls on sites whose protein changes strongly are the
least robust and are worth confirming by another method. Normalisation sets the reference of
usage: the default global centring removes a between-condition shift of the enriched fraction,
which is right when loading is not controlled but removes a genuine global change of
modification (for example after stimulation); per-condition centring is available for
experiments in which loading is controlled independently.

## Starting the interface

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(DiffPTM)
run_app()
```

The interface opens in the browser and runs on your computer: no data leave it. It is
organised in six steps, each a page of the left menu. Every step calls exported functions of
the package, so an analysis done in the interface can be reproduced in R from the saved
session (see the last section).

## 1. Import

Choose the software, upload the **total-proteome table** and the **PTM table** and click
*Import*. The formats accepted for each software are listed in the Help page and in the
vignettes *DiffPTM with MaxQuant*, *... with Spectronaut*, *... with Proteome Discoverer*,
*... with FragPipe* and *... with DIA-NN*.

Intensities are expected raw (the app applies log2). Untick *Intensities are raw* for tables
already on the log2 scale (FragPipe TMT-Integrator); the app warns when the scale looks wrong.

*Load example dataset* loads a simulated label-free experiment (1,500 proteins, 800
phosphosites, two conditions with four samples each) with its design, to try the interface.

## 2. Design

The Design page proposes a design as soon as the data are imported (`suggest_design()`). Its
rules use the data and the structure of the run names, not particular words, so that they apply
to MaxQuant, Spectronaut and DIA-NN exports alike; the page says in plain words what it did:

* runs without any quantified value are not used (a combined MaxQuant search lists every run in
  every table, including the runs of other enrichments);
* when both tables list the same runs (one search of enriched and total runs), the PTM-enriched
  runs are those that quantify many more sites than the others;
* a PTM run and a proteome run are paired when their names are the same once the parts that only
  mark the fraction are removed (`Phospho_mock_1` / `mock_1`; `P_R1-A` / `T_R1-A`;
  `Phospho-01_NS_R1` / `Proteome-01_NS_R1`; `..._Phos_Ctrl_01.raw` / `..._FP_Ctrl_01.raw`), or,
  failing that, when their names are clearly the most similar (`..._R1_Octobre` / `..._R1`).
  Paired runs receive the same **sample** name, which is what the usage test pairs on;
* each condition is read from the sample name without its replicate number, wherever it is
  (`mock_24h_1` -> `mock_24h`, `R1-A` -> `A`, `01_NS_R1` -> `NS`); MaxQuant SILAC channels become
  samples `L_<experiment>`, `H_<experiment>` with conditions `L` and `H`;
* when the conditions are all the combinations of two parts (`mock_6h`, `mock_24h`,
  `SARS_COV2_6h`, `SARS_COV2_24h`), they are split into a condition and a second factor, a
  time-like part (`6h`, `d3`, `T0`...) being the second factor (`split_factors()`): contrasts then
  compare the conditions within each time point. The page lets you swap the two factors or keep a
  single factor with all the groups.

Each table lists the **run** (column of the imported file), the **sample** name and the
**condition**; double-click a cell to change it (an empty condition means the run is not used).
A summary gives the number of proteome, PTM and paired samples per condition. Click
**Apply design** when it is right. *Advanced options*: renaming in bulk with a regular expression,
reading conditions from other parts of the names, a second factor and a subject, and the upload
of an annotation table (`run` or `sample`, `condition`, optional `factor`, `subject`, `mixture`).

Optional columns: a **second factor** (time point, batch; contrasts are built within each
level and ComBat can use it), a **subject** for paired designs across conditions (used as a
blocking factor) and the **TMT mixture**.

## 3. Processing

Every option is explained on the page; the defaults suit most data sets.

* *Filtering*: reverse hits, contaminants and "only identified by site" entries; site rows
  repeated for several protein accessions with identical quantities (Spectronaut); minimal
  localization probability (0.75); minimal number (and percentage) of observed values in at
  least one group (2).
* *PTM to protein matching*: by identifier (default; enough when both tables come from the same
  software and database) or by locating the peptide sequence in the FASTA of the search (when
  the two searches differ in protein inference or database version); *hybrid* uses the sequence
  when it gives a match, the identifier otherwise. The FASTA is needed for sequence or hybrid
  matching, and for peptide tables without site positions (DIA-NN precursors, FragPipe modified
  peptides), where it gives the position of the modified residue. A site that matches several
  quantified protein groups (shared peptide, isoforms) is corrected with their mean abundance
  (default), with the first one, or kept for the abundance test only.
* *Normalisation*: global median centering (default: removes differences of loading and of
  enrichment efficiency between samples); per-condition median centering (keeps a global shift
  between conditions; only when such a change is expected and loading was controlled
  independently, otherwise a loading difference becomes a change of every site); ComBat (batch
  = second factor); none (data already normalised by the software).
* *Imputation*: off by default; the tests use the observed values.

The **quality-control** plots show, for each table: the number of features observed per
sample (runs that quantified far fewer features than the others stand out and should be
removed in step 2), the intensity distributions, a PCA, the Pearson correlation matrix between
samples and the Jaccard index of detection between samples, both with the conditions as a
colour strip. The processing log lists every operation; it becomes the Materials & Methods
paragraph of the report.

## 4. Statistics

Choose the methods (the single model is always available; MSstatsPTM and msqrob2PTM when
installed), the analyses (protein abundance, PTM abundance, PTM usage), the contrasts (each
condition against a reference, every pair, or each condition against the others; with a second
factor, within each of its levels), the π₀-aware FDR procedure, the FDR threshold and an optional
fold-change threshold (1 = none, the recommended setting for usage). The analysis starts when
**Run** is clicked and the page reports the number of significant features per method. Running
times differ: for 21,770 sites and four contrasts on one thread, 12 s for the single model, about
a minute for msqrob2PTM and 11 min for MSstatsPTM.

## 5. Results

For the selected analysis, contrast and method: a volcano plot labelled with gene and site,
the raw p-value histogram (flat with a peak near 0 when the test is well calibrated), the
PTM-vs-protein fold-change plot (points off the diagonal change in usage), the number of
significant features per contrast and method, the agreement between methods as an UpSet plot
(each bar counts the features called by exactly the methods marked below it), the table of
significant features and the detection-discordance table (PTM features observed in samples
where their protein was not quantified, which no quantitative test can use).

## 6. Download

An Excel workbook with every table, a README sheet with the Materials & Methods paragraph and
a `column_descriptions` sheet that explains every column (also shown as comments on the column
headers of the result sheets); the figures as an editable PowerPoint and as PDF, quality control
first; and the session as an `.rds` file. The Materials & Methods text names the input files and
can be edited on the page before the Excel workbook is downloaded.

## Reproducing an interface analysis in R

The `.rds` session contains the processed experiment (`x`), the results (`res`), the
contrasts and the thresholds:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
s <- readRDS("DiffPTM_session.rds")
s$x                              # processed ptm_experiment, with its log
head(s$res)                      # tidy results: feature_id, analysis, contrast, log2FC, se, statistic, pvalue, adj_pvalue, method
cat(methods_paragraph(s$x, s$methods))
plot_volcano(subset(s$res, analysis == "ptm_DPU" & contrast == s$contrasts$name[1] & method == "limma"), s$fdr)
```

The same analysis from scratch, with the example dataset shipped in the package:

```{r example}
library(DiffPTM)
ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "DiffPTM")
prot <- import_protein(file.path(ex, "protein.tsv"), "Generic")
ptm  <- import_ptm(file.path(ex, "ptm.tsv"), "Generic")
ann  <- read_annotation(file.path(ex, "annotation.tsv"))
x <- new_ptm_experiment(prot, ptm, annotation = list(protein = ann, ptm = ann)) |>
  filter_localization(0.75) |> filter_min_observed(min_n = 2) |>
  normalise(method = "global_median") |> match_ptm_to_protein("id")
x
res <- run_methods(x, make_contrasts(x), methods = "limma", pi0_method = "bh")
table(res$analysis, res$adj_pvalue < 0.05)
```

```{r example-plots, fig.height = 5}
r <- subset(res, analysis == "ptm_DPU")
r$label <- x$ptm$meta$label[match(r$feature_id, x$ptm$meta$feature_id)]
plot_volcano(r, fdr = 0.05, title = "PTM usage, treated vs control")
```
